summary: Current main still allowed the DeepSeek-V4 CPU-tensor retraction backup's NotImplementedError to escape and terminate the decode scheduler. The correction converts only unsupported CPU-copy backups into the existing per-request backup-failure result, so retract_decode aborts the affected request while preserving existing behavior for supported pools and unrelated exceptions.

tests.what_was_measured: The issue-specific regression reproduced the uncaught NotImplementedError at retraction_backup; two boundary tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-216790ed0785/raw/regression-before.txt

Four tests passed: DSV4 inherits KVCache's unsupported get_cpu_copy stub, unsupported CPU backup returns False, supported backup returns True and is invoked once, and unrelated RuntimeError still propagates. Raw output: reports/j-216790ed0785/raw/regression-after.txt

Two existing GPU tests passed on gfx950, including numerical device-to-host backup and restore of supported target and draft MHA KV tensors plus host-pool exhaustion behavior. Raw output: reports/j-216790ed0785/raw/existing-gpu-backup-tests.txt
Changed Python files compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: Assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- was visible through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. Existing retraction backup GPU tests passed and numerically compared restored supported MHA target/draft KV buffers. Hardware and method evidence: reports/j-216790ed0785/raw/hardware-and-method-evidence.txt

remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4 weights and the reported tp8/dp8 multi-node PD deployment were unavailable; no full-model, semantic-accuracy, speculative MTP4, HiSparse-kernel, or distributed-load reproduction is claimed.

The assigned single gfx950 GPU validated supported backup/restore mechanics only. The DSV4 failure was reproduced deterministically at the actual retraction_backup implementation boundary using the pool's exact NotImplementedError contract.
This change contains the scheduler crash by aborting only the affected request; it does not add CPU-copy support for DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool or make unsupported DSV4 requests resumable.

An upstream open candidate, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36185, proposes broader host-pool support for a subset of non-speculative CUDA DSV4 layouts. It remains open and does not cover the reported speculative HiSparse configuration.
